depts.note: Kitchen timers are in Kitchen & Dining (B5); game and chess clocks in Toys & Games (E1).

b.w: Large display or visible disc for children.

s.t: Devices that count an interval up or down, such as the Time Timer, a stopwatch or an hourglass.
s.ax: kinds by how the interval shows: a count, a shrinking disc, falling sand

k.d: Hand-held instrument that measures an elapsed interval.

x.d: The page names the horologist Samuel Watson as maker of the first stopwatch; it gives no year.

k.nl: One entry is the origin of the kind; later stopwatches are commodity and are not entries.
k.sel: Follows Wikipedia's Stopwatch article. Complete: 1 of 1 in that article.

k.d: Countdown timer that shows remaining time as a shrinking coloured disc, made for children and focus work.

x.d: Countdown timer with a shrinking red disc, invented by Jan Rogers to help her youngest child change between routines.

k.nl: One entry is the origin of the kind; later visual timers are commodity.
k.sel: Follows the Time Timer company's own story, which dates the invention to almost thirty years ago without a year. Complete: 1 of 1 in that page.

k.d: Timepiece that measures an interval by sand running between two glass bulbs.

x.d: Ship's timekeeper; the earliest certain record is a receipt of about 1345 for the King's ship La George.

k.nl: One entry is the earliest documented form of the kind.
k.sel: Follows Wikipedia's Hourglass article. Complete: 1 of 1 in that article.

s.t: Instruments that tell the time of day from a shadow, for gardens, walls or the pocket.

k.d: Instrument that tells the time from the shadow of a gnomon: garden stand, wall, balcony or portable.

x.d: Oldest known sundial, from the Valley of the Kings, about 1500 BC.

k.nl: One entry is the origin of the kind.
k.sel: Follows Wikipedia's Sundial article. Complete: 1 of 1 in that article.

depts.t: Things that time an interval or tell the time from sun or sand; kitchen timers → Kitchen & Dining (B5), game clocks → Toys & Games (E1).
depts.ax: Does it measure an interval, or tell the time of day from the sun?

depts.note: Straps and modding parts are variety (sorted by compatibility); storage and clock parts are tier. Strap, bracelet and chain designs are attributes of their kinds, not entries.

b.v: movement family (NH35/NH36/NH34), dial diameter (28.5 mm), chapter ring, lug width
b.w: Modding parts are listed by what they fit.

b.v: sapphire > mineral > acrylic; 316L steel; FKM rubber
lug width and length; quick-release spring bars

s.t: What holds a watch to the wrist or pocket, such as a NATO strap, Jubilee bracelet or Albert chain.
s.ax: kinds by build: flexible strap, linked bracelet, chain

k.d: Band of leather, fabric or rubber made to hold a watch on the wrist; the NATO (G10) strap was developed by the UK Ministry of Defence and introduced in 1973.
Metal or integrated link band made to fit a watch case.
Chain (Albert chain, fob chain) made to attach a pocket watch.
see: the watch it is worn with

s.t: What keeps watches safe and running, such as a winder or watch roll.
s.ax: kinds by job: keep wound, keep safe

k.d: Powered stand that holds one automatic watch and keeps it wound.
Lined box, case or travel roll that stores and protects several watches.

s.t: Parts swapped to rebuild or customise a watch, such as an NH35 movement or SKX-style case.
s.ax: kinds from the inside out: movement, dial, hands, case, crystal, bezel, small parts

k.d: Movement (calibre) bought to fit, replace or upgrade in a watch; modders sort them by case and dial compatibility.

x.d: Eterna calibre of 1955 that is the base of the ETA 2824-2.
Swiss 28,800 vph hacking automatic in production since 1982, the benchmark mid-range calibre.
Swiss automatic chronograph calibre, Valjoux 7750 from the 1970s.
Sellita automatic, near-identical to the ETA 2824-2 with 26 jewels.
Automatic calibre from Swiss Technology Production, part of the Fossil Group.
Miyota automatic that is the base of the 9015.
Japanese 28,800 vph automatic of 2009, 0.6 mm thinner than the ETA 2824.
TMI/Seiko automatic calibres sold for watchmaking and modding: 21,600 vph, hacking, hand-winding.
Non-hacking 21-jewel automatic of the SKX and Seiko 5, discontinued 2019.
21,600 vph Seiko automatic with Spron mainspring; sold as NE15.
Chinese hand-wound chronograph calibre of Swiss origin, used in budget chronographs.

k.nl: One entry is a movement calibre or calibre family fitted by modders; revisions are versions.
k.sel: Follows Gear Patrol's guide to common automatic movements (all eight it names) plus four calibres from earlier pages (NH35/NH36, 7S26, 6R15, ST19); no whole-space list of calibres exists. Covers 8 of 8 calibres in Gear Patrol, and 4 others.

k.d: Dial made to be fitted to a watch.
Set of hands made to be fitted to a watch movement.
Case made to house a watch movement; modding cases are sold by the movement family they take.

x.d: Aftermarket case on the Seiko SKX007/SKX013 pattern, made for NH-family movements with a 28.5 mm dial and SKX chapter ring.
x.dt: 20 mm lugs · flat or double-domed sapphire · steel, aluminium or ceramic bezel insert, 60-minute or GMT 24-hour

k.nl: One entry is a named aftermarket case pattern.
k.sel: Follows Lucius Atelier's SKX case listing; no whole-space list exists. Complete: 1 of 1 in that page.

k.d: Glass, sapphire or plastic crystal made to cover a watch dial.
Rotating or fixed bezel and its graduated insert, swapped to change a watch's look or function.
see: the watch the bezel is fitted to

k.d: Clasps, spring bars and crowns sold separately to fit, repair or customise a watch.
Replacement parts for clocks: movements, pendulums, hands, dials, fit-up inserts and suspension springs.

depts.t: Things that hold, store, maintain or replace parts of a watch or clock; smartwatch bands → Phones, Tablets & Personal Devices (D2).
depts.ax: What does it do for the watch: hold it on the person, store it, or replace a part?
